why: Section 2.9 of the Math Review includes functions defined by cases and the square-root function; both appear in graph-reading and function-evaluation questions.
rule:
A **piecewise-defined** function uses a different formula on each part of its domain, for example $f(x)=\begin{cases}2x, & x\ge 0\\ 0, & x<0\end{cases}$. To evaluate it, first find which condition the input satisfies, then use that formula. Its graph is the pieces drawn side by side.

The absolute-value function is piecewise: $|x|=x$ for $x\ge0$ and $|x|=-x$ for $x<0$.

$g(x)=\sqrt{x}$ is defined only for $x\ge0$; its graph is the upper half of a parabola lying on its side, starting at the origin. $-\sqrt{x}$ is the lower half. The shifts of the previous lesson apply: $\sqrt{x}+c$ moves it up $c$, and $\sqrt{x+c}$ starts at $x=-c$.

examples.prompt: Find the domain and the intercepts of $g(x)=\sqrt{x+4}$.
steps: The radicand must satisfy $x+4\ge0$, so the domain is $x\ge-4$.

trap: Check which side of the break point the input is on, and which piece owns the break point itself ($x\ge1$ includes 1). For roots, $\sqrt{x+4}$ is defined for $x\ge-4$, not for $x\ge4$.

checks.stem: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x)=\begin{cases}3x, & x\ge 0\\ x+5, & x<0\end{cases}$ What is $f(-2)$?
What is the value of $x$ for which $\sqrt{x+3}=4$?
The smallest value of $x$ for which $\sqrt{x+9}$ is a real number is

choiceExplanations.B: $-3$ would be the boundary of $\sqrt{x+3}$... but here the radicand is $x+9$.
choiceExplanations.C: At $x=0$ the root is defined ($\sqrt9$), but smaller $x$ also work.
choiceExplanations.D: The root is defined well below 3.
choiceExplanations.E: The boundary is where $x+9=0$, which is $x=-9$, not $9$.
